frequency_question: How often do South Asian riparian governments successfully conclude major water treaty extensions or successors when executive will is present within the target timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes formal transboundary water resource agreements and renewals between South Asian states; excludes unilateral declarations or failed negotiations where executive will was absent.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty implementation mechanisms and minor adjustments
Teesta River interim sharing draft agreement consensus (pre-signing phase)

coverage_note: 4 major landmark cases identified in the modern democratic era of bilateral water talks involving India.
known_gaps: Minor sub-basin arrangements and informal state-level water sharing understandings are excluded to maintain focus on federal executive treaties.
skeleton: Enumerate major bilateral water negotiations in the region involving India and immediate riparians where executive mandates were tested.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 documented major attempts = 75 percent historical base rate for executive-driven riparian accords.
validity_reason: Bilateral hydro-diplomacy structures and federal executive decision-making frameworks in South Asia evolve slowly over decades.
